# Browser runtime dependencies

The application is plain JavaScript. Its shipped crypto and graphics dependencies
are tracked separately here because the root lockfile describes the Playwright
test runner. `inventory.json` records the exact browser files, source package,
license, size and SHA-256. The runtime package versions stay at Three.js 0.160.0
and Nostr Tools 2.10.3. The Three.js bundle is rebuilt with the pinned compiler
esbuild 0.28.2; its generated bytes change.

| Shipped files | Upstream | License | Reproduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `3d/three.min.js` | `three@0.160.0` | MIT | Bundle `3d/src/three-entry.js` with `esbuild@0.28.2`, minified IIFE with the `entry.cjs` wrapper semantics. Includes GLTFLoader, DRACOLoader and RoomEnvironment from the same release. |
| `3d/draco/draco_wasm_wrapper.js`, `3d/draco/draco_decoder.wasm` | glTF decoder distributed inside `three@0.160.0` | Apache-2.0 | Copy `examples/jsm/libs/draco/gltf/` from that exact package. |
| `nostr-tools.js` | `nostr-tools@2.10.3` | Unlicense; embedded @noble/@scure modules use MIT | Copy the official package's `lib/nostr.bundle.js`, without rebuilding or changing the crypto implementation. |

The original build's npm lockfile identified Three.js 0.160.0 and esbuild 0.20.2.
The original v66 Three.js bundle was first reproduced byte for byte with those
versions and `sourcefile: 'entry.cjs'`. This sourcefile setting preserves the
CommonJS wrapper semantics of the original build; a generic ESM entry produces
different output. The compiler was then upgraded to 0.28.2 to remove the known
esbuild development-server advisory [GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99).
This advisory concerns the old compiler's development server; it does not
establish a browser runtime compromise.

The current Three.js bundle SHA-256 is
`6685cc7c5a1fa3cfa6c663564345d7e53dc6a25ee1867141d2f7037ae63cc6c4`.
The historical v66 digest was
`2052258421898aaa54dd3e6c2dbd60b2909e847a9e6ea788795bf2426341210a`.
Nostr and Draco bytes are unchanged.

Draco is identified by its exact Three.js distribution and binary hashes. Its
independent Draco semantic version has not been established. The decoder README
in that distribution identifies the glTF branch and Apache-2.0 license. The full
[upstream license](https://github.com/google/draco/blob/main/LICENSE), including
its additional notices, was retrieved on 18 October 2026 and is preserved in
[`licenses/draco-Apache-2.0.txt`](licenses/draco-Apache-2.0.txt). This license
snapshot does not establish the decoder's separate release version.

## Reproduce and check

Use Node.js 20 or newer. Install the pinned development inputs once:

```sh
npm ci --prefix vendor --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
node tools/vendor-build.mjs --check
```

The check uses installed local packages and makes no network requests. It
compares the existing shipped files with the inventory, rebuilds Three.js,
reads the upstream Draco and Nostr bundles, and requires byte-for-byte matches.
It stops if provenance is incomplete or any file differs.

`node tools/vendor-build.mjs` writes matching candidates under
`artifacts/vendor-build/`. `--write` copies those verified candidates to their
runtime paths. Both verify all candidate bytes before writing. `--inventory`
only checks hashes of the existing files and needs no installed vendor packages;
it is not a reproduction test.

The Nostr prebuilt bundle is deliberately copied, not recreated using a newly
resolved dependency graph. The npm dependency graph records the upstream
package's dependency declarations; a fresh npm resolution of a semver range
cannot establish which transitive versions the publisher embedded in its bundle.
The pinned artifact hash establishes exactly which bytes ship in this app.

## Verification recorded on 18 October 2026

The root agent ran `check:vendor` successfully for all four runtime assets with
esbuild 0.28.2. The root and vendor npm audits each reported zero known
vulnerabilities in their resolved dependency trees. Evidence is retained locally
in `artifacts/security/root-audit.json` and
`artifacts/security/vendor-audit-final.json`; the earlier compiler finding is in
`artifacts/security/vendor-audit.json`. These results do not establish the exact
transitive versions embedded by the publisher in Nostr's prebuilt bundle, or a
separate Draco version. Browser regression checks are documented in the release
review rather than inferred from the vendor reproduction check.

## Maintenance and advisories

For each release, run the root tests, the vendor reproduction check, and both
`npm audit --prefix vendor` and `npm audit` in the root. Record the date and
results in the release review; a clean root audit alone does not cover vendored
runtime code. Review upstream release notes and advisories for Three.js, Draco,
Nostr Tools and the embedded `@noble` / `@scure` cryptographic dependencies.
Advisory absence is not a security certification.

For an update, pin the proposed exact package versions and regenerate this
lockfile. Review upstream provenance and licenses, build candidates in a separate
working directory, compare runtime changes, and deliberately update inventory
hashes only after review. Run encrypted synthetic chat round trips, hostile-input
checks, 3D guides, backup/restore, and installed-PWA upgrade/offline checks before
changing browser assets. Preserve the origin and all stored user data.

`3d/man.glb` is a separately licensed model asset, not an npm dependency; its
CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution and build procedure remain in `3d/LICENSE.md` and
`3d/src/README.md`.
